story.title: UN General Assembly Adopts New Map Reflecting Africa's True Size
story.summary: The United Nations General Assembly has voted to adopt a new world map that accurately represents Africa's size. Sponsored by Togo, the resolution received support from 164 member states, with the United States as the only nation voting against it. The new map replaces the traditional Mercator projection with the more accurate Equal Earth design from 2018.

explore_lenses.label: What does the UN vote actually change?
explore_lenses.title: A nonbinding push, not a mandated map swap
explore_lenses.summary: The September 4 resolution encourages wider use of Equal Earth and other area-accurate maps where comparative land area matters; it does not compel countries or private platforms to replace every Mercator map.

claims.text: The resolution does not ban Mercator or impose a single replacement; it encourages use of Equal Earth instead.
Togo said the initiative concerns proportional representation of land areas and does not alter, determine or recognize borders or territorial status.
Equal Earth preserves relative area, but no flat projection preserves every geographic property: equal-area maps necessarily trade off shape, angle, scale or direction.

explore_lenses.label: How did the Africa-led campaign reach the UN?
explore_lenses.title: AU endorsement preceded Togo’s UN initiative
explore_lenses.summary: The vote followed an African Union-backed campaign centered on how Mercator’s area distortion affects perceptions of Africa; Togo advanced the initiative for the African Group.

claims.text: The African Union says its heads of state and government endorsed the Correct the Map of Africa Initiative at their February 2026 assembly, after which Togo elevated it to the General Assembly.

The AU Commission characterized the aim as representing Africa and other regions on objective, scientifically established realities, while Togo’s Robert Dussey framed it as a matter of geographic knowledge, dignity and historical memory.
Mercator was designed for navigation and enlarges apparent areas toward the poles; in the commonly cited Africa-Greenland comparison, Africa is about 14 times Greenland’s actual area.

explore_lenses.label: Why was the vote not unanimous?
explore_lenses.title: U.S. opposition contrasted with broad support
explore_lenses.summary: The United States cast the only no vote, while six countries abstained. Supporters described the measure as a scientific and educational correction; the U.S. described it as ideological.

claims.text: The General Assembly vote on September 4 was 164 in favor, one against—the United States—and six abstentions: Estonia, Georgia, Lithuania, Moldova, Serbia and Ukraine.
According to UN News reporting, the U.S. dismissed the initiative as a “radical ideological project,” while Togo’s foreign minister said the debate was scientific rather than political.

The African Union Commission said it will work with Togo, member states and relevant partners to support implementation; this is a stated future plan, not a binding commitment by governments, schools or technology companies.

story_report.summary: The UN General Assembly adopted a Togo-sponsored resolution encouraging use of the Equal Earth world map projection, which preserves relative land area, rather than the traditional Mercator design. The measure passed on September 4 by 164 votes to one, with the United States opposed and six countries abstaining. It does not ban Mercator or impose a single mandatory map, but positions Equal Earth as the preferred alternative for portraying the relative size of land areas.

sections.heading: Mercator Distortion and Africa’s Size
sections.body: Mercator was designed for navigation and enlarges apparent areas closer to the poles. Africa is about 14 times Greenland’s actual area, although the two can appear broadly similar in size on Mercator maps. Equal Earth is an equal-area projection, meaning it preserves relative area, but no flat map can preserve every geographic property: gains in area accuracy require trade-offs involving shape, angles, scale or direction.

sections.heading: African Union Campaign Behind Resolution
sections.body: The African Union says its heads of state and government endorsed the Correct the Map of Africa Initiative at their February 2026 assembly, after which Togo brought the effort to the General Assembly. The AU Commission described the goal as representing Africa and other regions according to objective, scientifically established realities. Togo said the initiative concerns proportional land-area representation and does not determine borders, territorial status or recognition.

sections.heading: United States Opposes Map Initiative
sections.body: The United States was the sole vote against the resolution. According to UN News reporting, the U.S. described the initiative as a “radical ideological project,” while Togo’s foreign minister said the issue was scientific rather than political. Estonia, Georgia, Lithuania, Moldova, Serbia and Ukraine abstained; the consulted sources did not provide an explanation for each abstention.

unresolved.text: The consulted materials do not identify a UN enforcement mechanism, implementation timetable or common procurement standard for adopting Equal Earth maps. The African Union Commission has said it will work with Togo, member states and partners to support implementation, but that is a stated plan rather than a binding commitment by governments, schools or technology companies.
The evidence does not establish how much changing map projections alone would affect public perceptions or policy.

related_stories.title: US Envoys Discuss Peace Plans with Putin Before Meeting Zelenskyy in Kyiv
related_stories.summary: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff held talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow, discussing 'substantive plans' to end the war in Ukraine. Following the three-hour meeting, which was described as 'highly useful' by a Kremlin aide, the envoys traveled to Kyiv for further discussions with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Zelenskyy welcomed the envoys, emphasizing the importance of their visit amidst ongoing conflict.

related_stories.title: Escalating Tensions: Iran Claims Strike on US Vessel in Strait of Hormuz
related_stories.summary: Iran has claimed responsibility for striking an unmanned U.S. vessel attempting to enter the Strait of Hormuz, marking a significant escalation in hostilities between the two nations. The U.S. military has dismissed this claim, labeling it a 'total lie.' The Strait of Hormuz continues to be a critical flashpoint in the ongoing conflict.
